claims.text: Elemental composition governs superconducting behavior in high-entropy alloys.
The ratio of elements with high and low valence-electron counts governs superconducting behavior.
The ratio of elements with high and low valence-electron counts influences the density of states at the Fermi level.
Varying elemental composition changes the density of states at the Fermi level.
The density of states at the Fermi level influences superconducting critical temperature.
The density of states at the Fermi level influences superconducting critical current density.
Alloys with optimal ratios of high- and low-valence-electron elements will have higher superconducting critical temperatures than alloys with non-optimal ratios.
Alloys with optimal ratios of high- and low-valence-electron elements will have higher critical current densities than alloys with non-optimal ratios.
The proposed relationship is restricted to low-temperature and high-pressure conditions and to the investigated composition range.
